question: Germany brought in its first national minimum wage, €8.50 an hour, in 2015. What happened to the low-paid?
options: Pay rose; many moved to bigger firms
Pay barely rose; firms found loopholes
answer: Pay rose; many moved to bigger firms. Dustmann and colleagues found the minimum raised low wages without cutting overall employment, as low-paid workers shifted from small firms to larger, more productive ones, behind up to 17% of their wage gain. Other studies found losses in mini-jobs, part-time posts paying a few hundred euros a month.
move: Count where people move, not just who loses the old place.
trap: Expecting a wage floor to price the low-paid out of work.
source: Dustmann et al., Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2022
